1.  ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICIES.

At this Wal-Mart Process Facility, we utilize anhydrous ammonia that is considered hazardous by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).  The properties that make ammonia valuable as a refrigerant also necessitate certain safety precautions.  Wal-Mart strives to protect all its valuable resources and assets - both personnel and property.  We live and have families in this community.  We want to prevent exposure to all our personnel as well as nearby members of our community, existing natural resources, and the surrounding environment.  It is our policy to comply with all Federal, State, and Local regulations.  Through continual, accurate training and various safety devices and procedures, we work to minimize potential releases.

Our emergency response program has specific procedures for accidental releases of anhydrous ammonia as well as other emergencies.  We work in conjunction with the Lowndes County Emergency Management to prepare for necessary notification of all affected neighbors.

2. THE STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES HANDLED.

The primary purpose of our facility is the processing of fluid milk products and temporary refrigerated storage of the finished products.  We utilize anhydrous ammonia as the primary means for refrigeration.  An outside company is used to fill our storage receiver.  Piping then carries the ammonia to the needed refrigeration units.  Access to the site is restricted to facility employees, authorized management personnel and authorized contractors.
 
3. THE WORST CASE RELEASE SCENARIO(S) AND THE ALTERNATIVE RELEASE SCENARIO(S), INCLUDING ADMINISTRATIVE CONTROLS AND MITIGATION MEASURES TO LIMIT THE DISTANCES FOR EACH REPORTED SCENARIO.

Worst Case Release Scenario and the Alternative Release Scenario

Worst case and alternate release scenarios were developed using the methodology given in the EPAs RMP Comp program.  The details of the chosen scenarios are

located within the Risk Management Program that is located on site.

4. FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY.

This is a newly constructed facility that opened in June 2025.  At the time of this submission, the system had not been charged with ammonia.  Consequently, this Wal-Mart Process Facility has not incurred a reportable release.

5. THE RMP MANAGEMENT PROGRAM.

The management of the RMP program will be handled by the Maintenance Manager.  He/She will administrate in conjunction with the Wal-Mart Process Facility management and personnel.  Other entities or organizations that will be coordinated with include the Lowndes County Emergency Management.


6.  THE GENERAL ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND THE SPECIFIC PREVENTION STEPS.

The Wal-Mart Process Facility complies with all applicable Federal, State and Local regulations including the EPAs Accidental Release Prevention Rule.  Our personnel are trained about this during our Hazard Communications Training and through access to our Written Programs.  Our Refrigeration Maintenance operators receive a combination of classroom and On-The-Job training (OJT).  They are observed and are able to demonstrate proper job skills and knowledge.  Also, the ammonia system is operated, tested and maintained to the standard of International Institute of Ammonia Refrigeration, the most stringent standards of the industry.


7.  THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM.

Wal-Mart Process Facility has onsite Hazardous Materials trained personnel to immediately respond to adverse conditions.  We have monthly meetings as well as annual certification.  This helps minimize the potential of an off-site release. 

We work closely with the Lowndes County Emergency Management Agency on emergency preparedness.  We meet periodically with representatives the fire department to address any changes in the facility or any new concerns.

8. PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY.

Currently, Wal-Mart Process Facility trains and tests all refrigeration techni

cians.  Our preventive maintenance program is above standard and our total ammonia Process Safety Program is reviewed annually and updated periodically. Our program is improved continuously through annual update of our written program and annual training of our technicians.  We also take advantage of new technologies when safer and more economical alternatives are available.

Wal-Mart Process Facility has implemented the IIAR training protocol for their refrigeration technicians.  The program consists of classroom training, viewing various training/safety videos and written testing procedures.  The training will be conducted on at least an annual basis.
